text:
Thomas Chabot is doing his part for Ottawa from the back end: 10 points in 16 games, nine of them assists, and the Senators take 58% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, eight points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 29th of 215 defensemen in value last season, most of it from even-strength offense, and that's the same player this year.

The goals are missing (one, on 1.7 expected), which is nothing to worry about for a defenseman with this profile. What stands out more is the minutes: down more than five a night over his last ten, partly because of a game in Philadelphia in October where he played only 12. He has since settled back above 21 minutes, including 25 in the win over Colorado on Wednesday.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him last season against a typical 11%, and joining the rush more than most defensemen. Watch whether his minutes climb back to the 24 a night he usually carries.
headline: Chabot is setting up everything but scoring
